next_unit_hint: Three benchmark picks, in order: (1) TensorRT-LLM with tokens_per_block 128 vs 2 vs 16 (only engine that can put a reuse boundary inside a 64-block; build-time flag so each variant needs a re-engine + restart; arm64/GB10 + Qwen3.5-MoE support both unverified). (2) LMDeploy TurboMind with --enable-prefix-caching True and cache_block_seq_len=64 (cheapest same-quantum A/B; prefix caching ships OFF there; documented kernel matrix stops at sm90). (3) llama.cpp --cache-reuse 256 as the falsification test for 'no suffix recovery anywhere' (KV shifting, token-level, not block-aligned). Deliberately excluded: TGI (13x claim, but our model is not in its supported list), FastGen/MII (no prefix cache at all), Dynamo (needs a cluster; it is a router and inherits backend granularity). Also hand to whoever tunes SGLang: the 64-grid is more likely the hybrid-attention state cache (uses_mamba_radix_cache=true, max_mamba_cache_size=64) than the pager (page_size=1); decisive test = serve a dense model on the same deployment and re-measure the hit grid.
assumptions: 'GB10-class node' interpreted as one NVIDIA GB10 (Grace-Blackwell, arm64, sm_121-class, unified memory), no second node, no NVL72 fabric; used to judge runnability.

Added a fifth runnability value 'unverified' alongside the contract's yes/needs-restart/needs-cluster/not-supported-for-this-model: no vendor documents our exact Qwen3.5-MoE hybrid-attention variant, so guessing one of the four would have manufactured evidence.
